image.description: The image to create from. A create names exactly one of image and snapshot.

snapshot.description: The snapshot id or name to create from; it takes no command and no restart. A create names exactly one of image and snapshot.

implied.description: Set on a rule the policy did not write: dns when a name rule opened DNS, dns-rule when a dns rule did.

protocol.description: Absent for a rule over every protocol.

code.description: What a program matches on: invalid_request, body_too_large, not_found, sandbox_not_running, sandbox_not_stopped, sandbox_not_paused, sandbox_live, sandbox_failed, no_checkpoint, unsupported, in_use, name_taken, exec_exited, exec_running, exec_limit, no_app, app_ended, unauthorized, forbidden, timeout, command_not_started or internal. A later daemon may add a code, so a client must take one it does not know.

exit_code.description: The exit code of the command that never started, with command_not_started.

holders.description: The sandboxes or snapshots that hold the resource, with in_use.

message.description: A line for a human; match on code, never on this text.

status.description: cached and pulled carry reference and digest; pulling adds layers and bytes, the whole download; layer carries one layer's digest, bytes and present; unpacking carries reference, digest and layers; unpacked carries one layer's digest, layer and layers; building carries nothing more.

code.description: The exit code, or the code a command that never started ends with.

error.description: Why the command never started; absent when it started.

lost_bytes.description: The output bytes the buffer dropped before this client read them; absent when it dropped none.

signal.description: The signal that ended the command, or 0.

code.description: One of the codes of ErrorObject.code.

mode.description: The permission bits with setuid, setgid and sticky as a number, at most 0o7777 (4095); the type is in type.

signal.description: TERM or KILL, in capitals; absent or empty is TERM.

mode.description: The permission bits in octal, at most 0777; absent is 0755.

killed_at.description: When the host last ended the sandbox for its memory.

kills.description: Every time the host ended the sandbox for its memory.

restart_at.description: When the daemon starts the sandbox again; absent once a start ran or a stop called it off.

address.description: What the listener binds: 127.0.0.1, or 0.0.0.0 for a public forward.

error.description: Why a running sandbox's port does not listen, or else what the last connection hit.

listening.description: False while the sandbox is not running, or while the host refuses the port.

reachable_on.description: The IPv4 addresses of the host a client reaches the port on while it listens.

guest_port.description: The port on the sandbox's 127.0.0.1 a connection goes to.

host_port.description: The port on the host the forward listens on.

public.description: Listen on 0.0.0.0, every interface of the host, instead of 127.0.0.1.
Listen on 0.0.0.0, every interface of the host, instead of 127.0.0.1.

memory_mib.description: The memory bound in MiB. Absent, a create from a snapshot takes the snapshot's bound. Otherwise absent or 0 is 512 on the firecracker and vz providers, and no bound on gvisor, runc and sysbox.

backoff.description: The first wait before a restart, in seconds; 0 or absent is 1. It doubles after each restart, up to 60. Only on-failure and always take it.

retries.description: The restarts in a row before the policy gives up; 0 or absent is unlimited. Only on-failure takes it.

backoff.description: The first wait before a restart, in seconds; 0 or absent is 1. It doubles after each restart, up to 60. Only on-failure and always take it.

retries.description: The restarts in a row before the policy gives up; 0 or absent is unlimited. Only on-failure takes it.

protocol.description: Absent for a rule over every protocol.

destinations.description: The hosts the secret goes to. The first put of a name needs one; a rotation with none keeps the old ones.

size.description: The bytes the snapshot takes on the host disk; not disk_mib and not the logical size of its files.

info.description: The public routes of the shard daemon. shard serve checks a bearer token and its scope, named per operation as x-shard-scope; the daemon socket takes no token.
